## 1. Problem Summary

### 1.1 Regulatory context

Federal and state regulations impose hard turnaround deadlines on prior-authorization
decisions. Under the CMS 2024 Interoperability & Prior Authorization Final Rule
(CMS-0057-F), Medicare Advantage payers must respond:

- **72 hours** for urgent/expedited PA requests
- **7 calendar days** for standard PA requests
- **Within 24 hours** for appeal determinations on urgent cases (many state laws are
  stricter still)

State statutes add further constraints: Illinois SB 966, Maryland HB 1563, and similar
laws require faster decision windows for partially-automated and fully-automated PA
decisions, and mandate overturn-rate disclosure. These are the "statutory decision
clocks."

### 1.2 Current gaps

**Gap A — No clock tracking.**
The system captures submission timestamps (`AuditRecord.timestamp`) but does not model
the regulatory deadline window for each case. Coordinators cannot see how much time
remains on an open PA or appeal before a statutory violation occurs. The frontend
`Urgency` enum (`today / soon / later`) is assigned manually on demo fixtures; it is not
derived from any computed deadline.

**Gap B — Coordinator workflow is demo-only.**
`WorkflowPlan` (action, recipient, channel, turnaround) exists on `CriterionResult`
and is displayed in the queue workspace, but there is no backend endpoint to record
that a coordinator dispatched a workflow step, and no state transition is triggered by
that dispatch. The `awaiting_documentation` `CaseStatus` is unreachable from the live
backend — it exists in the enum and the frontend state machine but is never written by
any live API call.

**Gap C — Exception resolution has no backend write path.**
When a coordinator resolves an exception-tier case (overrides a `CriterionResult`
finding, dispatches a workflow), the only live path today is `POST /api/appeal/resume`
which re-enters the LangGraph graph at `hold`. That path requires `edited_text` — it
cannot record the coordinator's per-criterion decisions or trigger the
`awaiting_documentation` status branch. The two operations are orthogonal and must be
decoupled.

**Gap D — No compliance audit surface.**
Nothing today records whether a case was resolved before or after its statutory
deadline. `AuditRecord` has no deadline field; there is no API endpoint a compliance
dashboard can query to assess payer turnaround performance.

### 1.3 Why Slice 1, not later

The `TierRouter` (S3 Slice 2–3) already routes exception-tier cases to a human hold
queue. The HITL interrupt/resume backbone (S3 Slice 4a–4b) is live. The tenancy
scoping (P7a) is live. The coordinator workflow surface (queue workspace) is the next
live surface a real user will encounter. Statutory clocks must be computable before the
first real PA submission goes out; retrofitting them post-launch is a compliance risk,
not merely an engineering preference.

---

## 2. Goals

| ID | Goal | Success measure |
|----|------|-----------------|
| G1 | Compute and persist a statutory deadline for every PA and appeal case at submission time | `AuditRecord` carries `deadline_at` (ISO-8601 UTC) and `urgency_level` on every new write; existing records unaffected (additive schema) |
| G2 | Expose deadline data via a read-only, tenant-scoped API endpoint | `GET /api/cases/deadlines` returns `DeadlineRecord[]` filtered by tenant; p99 latency ≤ 100 ms on the in-memory store |
| G3 | Record coordinator workflow dispatch actions via the API | `POST /api/coordinator/dispatch` writes a `WorkflowDispatchRecord` and transitions the case to `awaiting_documentation` |
| G4 | Close the `awaiting_documentation` status gap — live backend writes this status | `CaseStatus.awaiting_documentation` is reachable from a live API call, not only from fixture data |
| G5 | Add a coordinator override path for exception-tier criterion resolution | `POST /api/coordinator/resolve` records per-criterion overrides and, if no open dispatch exists, advances the case to `ready_for_review` |
| G6 | All new fields parity-tested across `backend/models/schemas.py` ↔ `src/types.ts` | `test_schema_parity.py` + updated parity tests pass in CI with zero drift |
| G7 | Zero PHI in new log lines or API responses | New endpoints and audit records obey identifiers-only logging and the tokenized-patient-ref rule (ADR-0017) |

---

## 3. Non-Goals

| What | Why excluded |
|------|-------------|
| Automatic payer-facing clock notifications or escalations | Requires payer rail integration (Phase 2+); out of scope for Slice 1 |
| Clock computation for appeal round-2 or multi-round cases | Round-2 statutory windows differ by state and payer; deferred to a dedicated round-2 slice |
| Real CRD endpoint integration for urgency classification | CRD stub remains; urgency is derived from `InitialPaRequest.urgency_level` (caller-supplied with validation) |
| Frontend UI changes to the queue workspace visual | Slice 1 delivers backend + API only; the frontend coordinator UX is Slice 2 |
| PostgreSQL persistence | Durable audit store is a Phase 3 milestone; Slice 1 uses the existing in-memory store extended with new fields |
| Rate limiting or internet-facing deploy | Deferred per `08-deployment-ci.md` |
| Langfuse observability | Deferred per ADR-0007 |

---

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Functional requirements

#### FR-1  Deadline computation (server-side, deterministic)

The system MUST compute a `deadline_at` UTC timestamp for every case at the point the
first `AuditRecord` is written:

```
deadline_at = submission_timestamp + clock_window(lifecycle, urgency_level, jurisdiction)
```

Default clock windows (configurable via `backend/data/statutory_clocks.json` — see §5):

| Lifecycle    | Urgency    | Default window      |
|--------------|------------|---------------------|
| `initial_pa` | `urgent`   | 72 hours            |
| `initial_pa` | `standard` | 168 hours (7 days)  |
| `appeal`     | `urgent`   | 24 hours            |
| `appeal`     | `standard` | 720 hours (30 days) |

`jurisdiction` defaults to `federal` (CMS-0057-F). State-specific overrides are loaded
from `statutory_clocks.json` and applied when `plan_id` prefix matches a state-coded
payer (e.g., `IL-*` → Illinois, `MD-*` → Maryland). Missing prefix → `federal` fallback.

The computation MUST live in a new pure module `backend/utils/deadline.py`. It is not
a node, not a route handler, and contains no I/O after import. It is independently
unit-testable.

#### FR-2  Urgency level on requests

`InitialPaRequest` and `AppealRequest` gain an `urgency_level: UrgencyLevel` field
(new enum — see §5). The field is caller-supplied and validated; it drives FR-1.
Default `standard` when absent. Urgency is never inferred from clinical content (that
would require an LLM in a deterministic flow).

#### FR-3  Deadline written to AuditRecord

`AuditRecord` gains `deadline_at: datetime | None` and `urgency_level: UrgencyLevel |
None`. The `boundary.with_audit` wrapper MUST populate these from the computed value
before the terminal SSE event is emitted. Neither field is PII/PHI; they are metadata.

#### FR-4  GET /api/cases/deadlines

A new read-only, tenant-scoped, authenticated endpoint listing open cases with their
deadline status. Response includes `clock_status: ClockStatus` enum
(`running | expired | paused`) derived at read time — computed from `deadline_at` vs
`now`, never stored. See §6 for the full contract.

#### FR-5  POST /api/coordinator/dispatch

An authenticated, CSRF-protected endpoint that:

1. Accepts a `WorkflowDispatchRequest` identifying a `correlation_id` + a list of
   `WorkflowDispatchItem` (one per `CriterionResult` that carries a `WorkflowPlan`).
2. Writes a `WorkflowDispatchRecord` to the coordinator-plane audit store.
3. Transitions the case `CaseStatus` to `awaiting_documentation`.
4. Returns `204`.

This gives the existing demo-only `WorkflowPlan` UI its live write path.

#### FR-6  POST /api/coordinator/resolve

An authenticated endpoint that:

1. Accepts a `CoordinatorResolveRequest` identifying a `correlation_id` + a list of
   `CriterionOverride` (each with `rule_label`, `override_status: CriterionStatus`,
   `rationale: str`).
2. Validates that the `correlation_id` corresponds to a parked exception-tier run.
3. Checks whether any `WorkflowDispatchRecord` exists for the `correlation_id`:
   - If yes → `resulting_status = CaseStatus.awaiting_documentation`,
     `pending_workflows = True`
   - If no → `resulting_status = CaseStatus.ready_for_review`,
     `pending_workflows = False`
4. Writes a `CoordinatorResolveRecord`.
5. Returns `200 CoordinatorResolveResponse`.

**Does NOT resume the LangGraph graph.** The graph stays parked.
`POST /api/appeal/resume` remains the path that re-enters the graph with `edited_text`.
These are orthogonal operations.

#### FR-7  Security and tenancy invariants

All new endpoints MUST:

- Be gated by the dual-auth middleware (Bearer or `paxos_session` cookie) before body
  parse — a bad token gets `401`, never `422`.
- Cookie-authenticated writes carry `X-CSRF-Token` (double-submit CSRF defense); missing
  or invalid token → `403`.
- Read paths apply the fail-closed `TenancyScope` at the store query boundary
  (ADR-0017).
- Write paths stamp `tenant_id` from `request.state.tenancy_scope` onto new records.
- Log identifiers only (`correlation_id`, `tenant_id`, `scenario_id`) — never
  request/letter text, never the `patient_ref` value.

#### FR-8  Statutory clock config file

`backend/data/statutory_clocks.json` — new versioned file (not from
`pa_requirements.json`):

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "source_note": "Engineering approximation of CMS-0057-F, IL SB 966, MD HB 1563. Consult legal before relying on for compliance.",
  "federal": {
    "initial_pa": { "urgent": 72,  "standard": 168 },
    "appeal":     { "urgent": 24,  "standard": 720 }
  },
  "state_overrides": {
    "IL": { "initial_pa": { "urgent": 24, "standard": 72 } },
    "MD": { "initial_pa": { "urgent": 24, "standard": 72 } }
  },
  "plan_id_state_prefix_map": {
    "IL-":      "IL",
    "MD-":      "MD",
    "CIGNA-IL": "IL"
  }
}
```

All values are **hours** (integers). Loaded once at module import in
`backend/utils/deadline.py`, validated with Pydantic at load time, raises `ETLParseError`
on malformed config (consistent with `retrieval.py`'s handling of `pa_requirements.json`).
The file is NOT generated — it is authored and version-controlled.

### 4.2 Non-functional requirements

| ID    | Requirement |
|-------|-------------|
| NFR-1 | New modules follow CLAUDE.md File Organization: no business logic in route handlers; nodes stay `(state) → state` pure; no new inline type definitions |
| NFR-2 | `deadline.py` has 100% branch coverage in unit tests (small, pure module — tractable) |
| NFR-3 | All new Pydantic models use `ConfigDict(strict=True)` consistent with the existing models |
| NFR-4 | `statutory_clocks.json` changes are additive — no removal of existing keys without a migration note in the PR |
| NFR-5 | New enum values added to both `backend/models/schemas.py` and `src/types.ts` in the same commit; `test_schema_parity.py` updated in the same commit |
| NFR-6 | `wire-types-freshness` CI job continues to pass — `openapi.json` and `src/generated/api-types.d.ts` regenerated and committed |
| NFR-7 | No new dependency without the CLAUDE.md pre-install protocol; `statutory_clocks.json` parsing uses stdlib `json` + Pydantic — no new package needed |

---

## 5. Data Model Changes

### 5.1 New enums — `backend/models/schemas.py` (+ `src/types.ts` mirror)

```python
class UrgencyLevel(str, Enum):
    """Caller-supplied urgency classification driving the statutory clock window."""
    urgent   = "urgent"
    standard = "standard"

class ClockStatus(str, Enum):
    """Derived at read time from deadline_at vs now. Never persisted."""
    running = "running"   # deadline_at is in the future
    expired = "expired"   # deadline_at is in the past, case not resolved
    paused  = "paused"    # case status is awaiting_documentation (clock paused per CMS rule)
```

`CaseStatus` already contains `awaiting_documentation` — no change needed.

**`src/types.ts` mirror:**

```typescript
export type UrgencyLevel = "urgent" | "standard";
export type ClockStatus  = "running" | "expired" | "paused";
```

### 5.2 Modified models — `backend/models/schemas.py`

#### `AppealRequest` — additive fields

```python
class AppealRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    # ... all existing fields unchanged ...
    urgency_level: UrgencyLevel = UrgencyLevel.standard
```

#### `InitialPaRequest` — additive fields

```python
class InitialPaRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    # ... all existing fields unchanged ...
    urgency_level: UrgencyLevel = UrgencyLevel.standard
```

Both default to `standard` — existing callers that omit the field are unaffected
(backward-compatible additive change).

#### `AuditRecord` — additive fields

```python
class AuditRecord(BaseModel):
    # ... all existing fields unchanged ...
    deadline_at:   datetime | None = None       # UTC; None for pre-Slice-1 records
    urgency_level: UrgencyLevel | None = None   # None for pre-Slice-1 records
```

`None`-defaulted: existing in-memory records remain valid; no migration needed pre-DB.

### 5.3 New models — `backend/models/schemas.py`

#### `DeadlineRecord` (read model, never persisted)

```python
class DeadlineRecord(BaseModel):
    correlation_id: str
    scenario_id:    str
    drug:           str
    plan:           str
    lifecycle:      CaseLifecycle
    urgency_level:  UrgencyLevel
    deadline_at:    datetime          # UTC ISO-8601
    clock_status:   ClockStatus       # computed at read time, never stored
    submitted_at:   datetime          # AuditRecord.timestamp
    tenant_id:      str
    patient_ref:    str | None = None # tokenized PT-XXXX if present
```

#### `DeadlineRecordsResponse`

```python
class DeadlineRecordsResponse(BaseModel):
    records: list[DeadlineRecord]
```

#### `WorkflowDispatchItem`

```python
class WorkflowDispatchItem(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    rule_label:  str  # matches CriterionResult.rule.label
    action:      str  # from WorkflowPlan.action
    recipient:   str  # from WorkflowPlan.recipient
    channel:     str  # from WorkflowPlan.channel
    turnaround:  str  # from WorkflowPlan.turnaround
```

#### `WorkflowDispatchRequest`

```python
class WorkflowDispatchRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    correlation_id: str                          # 1–200 chars
    dispatches:     list[WorkflowDispatchItem]   # non-empty
```

#### `WorkflowDispatchRecord` (coordinator-plane audit record)

```python
class WorkflowDispatchRecord(BaseModel):
    correlation_id:  str
    tenant_id:       str
    dispatched_by:   str       # session user_id, or "" for Bearer
    dispatched_at:   datetime  # UTC
    dispatches:      list[WorkflowDispatchItem]
    idempotency_key: str       # f"{correlation_id}:dispatch"
```

#### `CriterionOverride`

```python
class CriterionOverride(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    rule_label:      str              # matches CriterionResult.rule.label
    override_status: CriterionStatus  # found | needs_review | conflict
    rationale:       str              # min_length=1, max_length=500; required
```

#### `CoordinatorResolveRequest`

```python
class CoordinatorResolveRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    correlation_id: str                        # 1–200 chars
    overrides:      list[CriterionOverride]    # non-empty
```

#### `CoordinatorResolveRecord` (coordinator-plane audit record)

```python
class CoordinatorResolveRecord(BaseModel):
    correlation_id:    str
    tenant_id:         str
    resolved_by:       str        # session user_id, or ""
    resolved_at:       datetime   # UTC
    overrides:         list[CriterionOverride]
    pending_workflows: bool       # True if open WorkflowDispatchRecord exists
    resulting_status:  CaseStatus # awaiting_documentation | ready_for_review
    idempotency_key:   str        # f"{correlation_id}:resolve"
```

#### `CoordinatorResolveResponse`

```python
class CoordinatorResolveResponse(BaseModel):
    correlation_id:    str
    case_status:       CaseStatus
    pending_workflows: bool
```

### 5.4 New utility module — `backend/utils/deadline.py`

Pure module (no I/O after import). All functions synchronous, no side effects.

```python
# Public API
def load_clock_config() -> ClockConfig
    # Called once at module import.
    # Raises ETLParseError on malformed JSON.

def compute_deadline(
    submission_at: datetime,
    lifecycle: CaseLifecycle,
    urgency: UrgencyLevel,
    plan_id: str,
) -> datetime
    # Returns a timezone-aware UTC datetime.
    # All deadline_at values are UTC-aware — tzinfo is never None.

def compute_clock_status(
    deadline_at: datetime,
    case_status: CaseStatus,
    now: datetime,
) -> ClockStatus
    # Derived at read time, never stored.
    # awaiting_documentation → paused regardless of deadline_at.
    # past deadline + not paused → expired.
    # future deadline + not paused → running.

def resolve_jurisdiction(plan_id: str) -> str
    # Returns "federal" or a state code ("IL", "MD", …).
    # Pure — reads only the loaded config.
```

`ClockConfig` is a private Pydantic model used only inside `deadline.py` to validate
the JSON at load time. It is **not** exported from `models/schemas.py`.

**Pausing semantics:** `CaseStatus.awaiting_documentation` pauses the clock per
CMS-0057-F §84.1(b) — a case waiting on provider-submitted documentation is not
chargeable against the payer's turnaround window. `compute_clock_status` returns
`ClockStatus.paused` whenever `case_status == awaiting_documentation`, regardless of
whether `deadline_at` is in the past.

### 5.5 New audit store extension — `backend/audit/store.py`

The existing `AuditStore` manages `list[AuditRecord]`. It gains two new private lists
and the following methods:

```python
def record_workflow_dispatch(record: WorkflowDispatchRecord) -> None
    # Idempotent on idempotency_key.
    # Duplicate key → no-op + WARNING log (identifiers only).

def record_coordinator_resolve(record: CoordinatorResolveRecord) -> None
    # Idempotent on idempotency_key.

def pending_dispatches_for(
    correlation_id: str, scope: TenancyScope
) -> list[WorkflowDispatchRecord]

def resolve_records_for(
    correlation_id: str, scope: TenancyScope
) -> list[CoordinatorResolveRecord]

def deadline_records(scope: TenancyScope) -> list[AuditRecord]
    # Returns only AuditRecords where deadline_at is not None.
    # Pre-Slice-1 records (deadline_at is None) are silently excluded.
```

All query methods require a `TenancyScope` argument (fail-closed, ADR-0017).

**Important:** `WorkflowDispatchRecord` and `CoordinatorResolveRecord` are stored in
separate lists, not mixed into `list[AuditRecord]`. They are coordinator-plane records,
not pipeline boundary records. The existing `all_records()` method and its callers are
unaffected.

### 5.6 New coordinator logic module — `backend/agents/coordinator.py`

Business logic for the two new write operations. Route handlers in `main.py` are
logic-free; they delegate here (CLAUDE.md File Organization).

```python
def build_dispatch_record(
    request: WorkflowDispatchRequest,
    scope: TenancyScope,
    session_user_id: str,
) -> WorkflowDispatchRecord

def build_resolve_record(
    request: CoordinatorResolveRequest,
    scope: TenancyScope,
    session_user_id: str,
    store: AuditStore,
) -> CoordinatorResolveRecord
    # Calls store.pending_dispatches_for to determine pending_workflows.
    # Calls is_run_parked(request.correlation_id) to confirm parked state.
    # Raises LookupError (→ 404) if no exception-tier done record found.
```

No I/O inside functions except store reads (which use the injected `AuditStore`).

### 5.7 Frontend parity contract — `src/types.ts`

Add in the same commit as `backend/models/schemas.py` changes:

```typescript
export type UrgencyLevel = "urgent" | "standard";
export type ClockStatus  = "running" | "expired" | "paused";

export interface DeadlineRecord {
  correlationId:  string;
  scenarioId:     string;
  drug:           string;
  plan:           string;
  lifecycle:      CaseLifecycle;
  urgencyLevel:   UrgencyLevel;
  deadlineAt:     string;       // ISO-8601 UTC
  clockStatus:    ClockStatus;
  submittedAt:    string;
  tenantId:       string;
  patientRef?:    string;
}

export interface WorkflowDispatchItem {
  ruleLabel:   string;
  action:      string;
  recipient:   string;
  channel:     string;
  turnaround:  string;
}

export interface CoordinatorResolveResponse {
  correlationId:    string;
  caseStatus:       CaseStatus;
  pendingWorkflows: boolean;
}
```

The existing `WorkflowPlan` interface is unchanged — `WorkflowDispatchItem` is its
API wire form.

`test_schema_parity.py` must be updated to cover `UrgencyLevel` and `ClockStatus`.

## 6. API Changes

### 6.1 Route summary

| Method | Path | Auth | Body | Response | Status |
|--------|------|------|------|----------|--------|
| `GET`  | `/api/cases/deadlines`        | Bearer or cookie           | —                           | `DeadlineRecordsResponse`    | ✅ New |
| `POST` | `/api/coordinator/dispatch`   | Bearer or cookie + CSRF    | `WorkflowDispatchRequest`   | `204`                        | ✅ New |
| `POST` | `/api/coordinator/resolve`    | Bearer or cookie + CSRF    | `CoordinatorResolveRequest` | `CoordinatorResolveResponse` | ✅ New |
| `POST` | `/api/appeal/generate`        | existing                   | `AppealRequest`             | existing                     | ⚠️ `urgency_level` added |
| `POST` | `/api/pa/submit`              | existing                   | `InitialPaRequest`          | existing                     | ⚠️ `urgency_level` added |

### 6.2 GET /api/cases/deadlines

**Auth:** dual scheme. Cookie session sees only its tenant's records (fail-closed
`TenancyScope`). Bearer/platform sees all.

**Query params:** none in Slice 1 (pagination deferred to Phase 3 alongside PostgreSQL).

**Response:** `200 application/json`

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "correlation_id": "ozempic-cigna-clinical-pa:a1",
      "scenario_id": "ozempic-cigna-clinical-pa",
      "drug": "Ozempic (semaglutide)",
      "plan": "Cigna Connect 360",
      "lifecycle": "initial_pa",
      "urgency_level": "standard",
      "deadline_at": "2026-07-26T13:50:00+00:00",
      "clock_status": "running",
      "submitted_at": "2026-07-19T13:50:00+00:00",
      "tenant_id": "tenant_demo",
      "patient_ref": "PT-0042"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Clock status derivation** is performed in the route handler for each record:

1. Look up the `CoordinatorResolveRecord` for the `correlation_id` (if any).
2. If `resulting_status == ready_for_review` → omit the record entirely (case resolved).
3. If `resulting_status == awaiting_documentation` → pass `awaiting_documentation` as
   `case_status` to `compute_clock_status`.
4. Otherwise → pass `processing` as `case_status`.

**Filtering:** only `AuditRecord`s where `deadline_at is not None` are included.
Pre-Slice-1 records are excluded silently.

**Error responses:** `401` missing credential; `403` N/A (GET).

### 6.3 POST /api/coordinator/dispatch

**Auth:** dual scheme. Cookie write requires `X-CSRF-Token`. Bearer: `dispatched_by = ""`.

**Request body:** `WorkflowDispatchRequest`

**Validation:**
- `correlation_id` 1–200 chars (Pydantic `min_length=1, max_length=200`).
- `dispatches` non-empty (`min_length=1`).
- Each `WorkflowDispatchItem` field non-empty.

**Processing** (delegated to `backend/agents/coordinator.py`, not `main.py`):

1. Call `build_dispatch_record(request, scope, session_user_id)`.
2. Call `store.record_workflow_dispatch(record)` — idempotent.
3. Return `204`.

**No LangGraph interaction.** Graph stays parked; `hold` node untouched.

**Error responses:**

| Code | Cause |
|------|-------|
| `400` | `dispatches` is empty or `correlation_id` is blank |
| `401` | No valid credential |
| `403` | Missing or invalid CSRF token on cookie-auth request |
| `422` | Body validation failure (Pydantic) |

### 6.4 POST /api/coordinator/resolve

**Auth:** dual scheme. Cookie write requires `X-CSRF-Token`.

**Request body:** `CoordinatorResolveRequest`

**Validation:**
- `correlation_id` 1–200 chars.
- `overrides` non-empty.
- Each `CriterionOverride.rationale` non-empty (`min_length=1`), ≤ 500 chars.

**Processing** (delegated to `backend/agents/coordinator.py`):

1. Confirm `correlation_id` has an exception-tier `done` `AuditRecord` in this
   tenant's scope. If not found → `404`.
2. Check `is_run_parked(correlation_id)` (`agents/review_queue.py`). If not parked →
   `404`.
3. Check `store.pending_dispatches_for(correlation_id, scope)`:
   - Any exist → `pending_workflows = True`,
     `resulting_status = CaseStatus.awaiting_documentation`.
   - None → `pending_workflows = False`,
     `resulting_status = CaseStatus.ready_for_review`.
4. Check idempotency: if `CoordinatorResolveRecord` already exists for
   `idempotency_key = f"{correlation_id}:resolve"` → return `200` from the existing
   record without writing a second.
5. Call `store.record_coordinator_resolve(record)`.
6. Return `200 CoordinatorResolveResponse`.

**Error responses:**

| Code | Cause |
|------|-------|
| `400` | `overrides` empty or any `rationale` blank |
| `401` | No valid credential |
| `403` | Missing or invalid CSRF token |
| `404` | `correlation_id` has no exception-tier done record in this tenant's scope, or run is not parked |
| `422` | Body validation failure |

### 6.5 Modified: POST /api/appeal/generate and POST /api/pa/submit

`urgency_level: UrgencyLevel = UrgencyLevel.standard` added to `AppealRequest` and
`InitialPaRequest`. Default of `standard` makes this backward-compatible — existing
callers that omit the field work unchanged.

The `AuditRecord` written at the pipeline boundary (`backend/audit/boundary.py`) MUST
call `compute_deadline` and set `record.deadline_at` and `record.urgency_level` before
the write. Integration point detail is in §7.5.

The SSE event shapes (`DoneEvent`, `InitialPaDoneEvent`) are **not changed** — deadline
data is an audit-plane concern, queryable via `GET /api/cases/deadlines`, not streamed.

### 6.6 OpenAPI registration

New endpoints and new model shapes must be registered in `backend/openapi_ext.py`
following the existing pattern (same as existing SSE event shapes). After
implementation:

```bash
npm run api:dump && npm run api:types
```

Commit the updated `openapi.json` and `src/generated/api-types.d.ts`. The
`wire-types-freshness` CI job must pass.

---

## 7. LangGraph Integration

### 7.1 No new graph nodes in Slice 1

Slice 1 does not add, remove, or reorder any node in `agents/graph.py` or
`agents/initial_pa_graph.py`. Coordinator resolution and dispatch are coordinator-plane
operations — they interact with the audit store and coordinator records, not the
LangGraph state machine.

### 7.2 Interaction with the existing hold node

The existing `hold` node calls `interrupt()` after `finalize` emits the `DoneEvent` for
exception-tier runs. This behavior is **unchanged**.

`POST /api/coordinator/resolve` calls `is_run_parked(correlation_id)` (from
`agents/review_queue.py`) to confirm the run is still parked before writing any record.
This is the same public API that `run_resume` uses — it survives the Phase 3 PostgreSQL
checkpointer swap (ADR-0010 note).

Resulting status by case:

| Parked? | Open dispatch? | `resulting_status` |
|---------|---------------|-------------------|
| Yes     | No            | `ready_for_review` |
| Yes     | Yes           | `awaiting_documentation` |
| No      | —             | `404` |

### 7.3 The LangGraph checkpoint is not touched by resolve

The resolve endpoint records the coordinator's per-criterion decisions. Resuming the
graph remains a separate, explicit `POST /api/appeal/resume` call. This separation means:

1. A coordinator can record criterion overrides before a reviewer supplies `edited_text`.
2. The `human_edited` `AuditRecord` written by `run_resume` correctly reflects letter
   sign-off, independently of the coordinator's criterion decisions.
3. `GET /api/reviews/pending` continues to show the run as pending until
   `POST /api/appeal/resume` is called — correct: a run is not review-cleared until the
   letter is signed off.

### 7.4 PipelineState and InitialPaState: no changes

Neither TypedDict is modified. Urgency and deadline are audit-plane data, not
pipeline-state data. The pipeline computes letters; the audit boundary records outcomes.
These are separate planes.

### 7.5 Audit boundary integration point — `backend/audit/boundary.py`

This is the only place `compute_deadline` is called — never in a node, never in a
route handler.

```python
# Inside the boundary write logic, after the terminal event is determined,
# before store.write(record):

from backend.utils.deadline import compute_deadline

deadline_at = compute_deadline(
    submission_at=record.timestamp,
    lifecycle=record.lifecycle,
    urgency=request.urgency_level,    # UrgencyLevel from the originating request
    plan_id=request.plan_id,
)
record = record.model_copy(update={
    "deadline_at":   deadline_at,
    "urgency_level": request.urgency_level,
})
store.write(record)
# then emit terminal SSE event
```

**Implementation note (Risk R1):** `boundary.py` currently receives only `AuditRecord`,
not the originating request. Preferred approach: pass `urgency_level` and `plan_id` as
explicit parameters to the boundary write call. Alternative: derive from fields already
on `AuditRecord` (but `urgency_level` is not yet there, so this is circular). Choose at
implementation time and note the decision in a PR comment.

---

## 9. Risks & Mitigations

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|----|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| R1 | **Audit boundary signature change.** Adding `request.urgency_level` to the boundary write requires the originating request inside `boundary.py`, which today receives only `AuditRecord`. | Medium | Medium | Preferred: pass `urgency_level` and `plan_id` as explicit parameters to the boundary write call. Alternative: thread them through `AuditRecord` fields populated earlier in the call stack. Choose at implementation time; document decision in PR. |
| R2 | **`is_run_parked` imported by `coordinator.py`.** `agents/review_queue.py` is currently consumed only by `main.py`. A cross-module import is a minor coupling risk. | Low | Low | Consistent with the existing pattern (split for testability; `review_queue.py` is already the public API for parked-run checks). Document the import. |
| R3 | **Clock windows are a policy interpretation, not law text.** Specific hour values may not reflect the current statute (statutes change). | Medium | High | `statutory_clocks.json` is a versioned, human-readable file with a `source_note` field and a file-header comment: "Engineering approximation — consult legal before relying on for compliance." All updates go through a PR with a legal-review note. |
| R4 | **Store thread-safety (pre-DB).** New store lists carry the same single-worker caveat as the existing `AuditRecord` list (no lock today, ADR-0009). | Low | Low | Do not introduce a new locking mechanism — that is architectural scope creep. Single-worker caveat stands per ADR-0009. |
| R5 | **Coordinator dispatch vs `GET /api/reviews/pending` UX confusion.** After dispatch, the case has `awaiting_documentation` in the resolve record, but `GET /api/reviews/pending` still shows it as pending (graph is still parked). | Medium | Medium | By design (§7.3): a pending review means "awaiting `POST /api/appeal/resume`", not "awaiting coordinator resolution". Document this distinction in the route description; the Slice 2 frontend UX will differentiate the two states visually. |
| R6 | **`deadline_at` timezone bugs.** Naive datetime arithmetic silently produces wrong deadlines. | Medium | High | `compute_deadline` uses `datetime.timezone.utc` throughout. All `deadline_at` values stored and returned as UTC ISO-8601 with explicit `tzinfo`. Tests assert `deadline.tzinfo is not None`. |

---

### 10.3 ADR-0018 — `backend/docs/adr/0018-statutory-decision-clocks.md`

Must cover:

- Decision to compute deadline at the audit boundary (not in a pipeline node) and why.
- Decision to store clock config in a versioned JSON file (not DB or env vars) and why.
- Decision to pause the clock on `awaiting_documentation` only, not all hold states.
- Decision to keep `WorkflowDispatchRecord` and `CoordinatorResolveRecord` in separate
  store lists from `AuditRecord` (coordinator-plane vs pipeline-plane records).
- Decision to keep `POST /api/coordinator/resolve` and `POST /api/appeal/resume`
  orthogonal (why resolve does not resume the graph).

### 10.4 CI gates — all must be green on the feature branch

| Gate | What it checks |
|------|----------------|
| `backend-unit` | All existing + 2 new unit test modules pass |
| `backend-integration` | All existing + 1 new integration test module pass |
| `frontend-check` | `npm test` passes (`src/types.ts` updated in same commit) |
| `wire-types-freshness` | `openapi.json` + `src/generated/api-types.d.ts` are fresh |
| `lint` | `ruff check .` + `mypy . --ignore-missing-imports` pass |
| `pip-audit` | No new CVEs introduced |

### 10.5 TDD commit sequence

```
1. schema(slice1):  add UrgencyLevel, ClockStatus enums; add fields to
                    AppealRequest, InitialPaRequest, AuditRecord; add 7 new
                    models; update src/types.ts + test_schema_parity.py
                    → CI: RED on new parity assertions (expected)

2. test(slice1):    RED — backend/tests/unit/test_deadline_utils.py

3. feat(slice1):    GREEN — backend/utils/deadline.py +
                    backend/data/statutory_clocks.json

4. test(slice1):    RED — backend/tests/unit/test_coordinator.py

5. feat(slice1):    GREEN — backend/agents/coordinator.py

6. feat(slice1):    wire audit boundary: compute_deadline called in
                    backend/audit/boundary.py

7. test(slice1):    RED — backend/tests/integration/test_coordinator_endpoints.py
                    (includes test_sse_endpoint.py additions)

8. feat(slice1):    GREEN — 3 new routes in main.py + openapi_ext.py +
                    backend/audit/store.py extensions

9. chore(slice1):   npm run api:dump && npm run api:types → commit
                    openapi.json + src/generated/api-types.d.ts

10. docs(slice1):   backend/docs/adr/0018-statutory-decision-clocks.md
```

### 10.6 Acceptance criteria (human reviewer checklist)

- [ ] `GET /api/cases/deadlines` returns records with correct `deadline_at` computed
      from `urgency_level` and `plan_id` prefix matching.
- [ ] `clock_status = paused` returned when a `CoordinatorResolveRecord` exists with
      `resulting_status = awaiting_documentation`.
- [ ] Resolved-to-`ready_for_review` cases are absent from
      `GET /api/cases/deadlines`.
- [ ] `POST /api/coordinator/dispatch` returns `204`; dispatch is retrievable under
      the correct tenant scope only.
- [ ] `POST /api/coordinator/resolve` with an open dispatch → `200`,
      `case_status = awaiting_documentation`.
- [ ] `POST /api/coordinator/resolve` with no open dispatch → `200`,
      `case_status = ready_for_review`.
- [ ] `POST /api/coordinator/resolve` with unknown `correlation_id` → `404`.
- [ ] `POST /api/appeal/generate` with `urgency_level: "urgent"` produces an
      `AuditRecord` with `deadline_at = submission_time + 24h` (±1 s tolerance).
- [ ] Cookie-authenticated POST to any new endpoint without `X-CSRF-Token` → `403`.
- [ ] Cookie session scoped to `tenant_demo` cannot see another tenant's records from
      `GET /api/cases/deadlines`.
- [ ] All CI gates are green on the feature branch.
- [ ] No PHI in any new log line (manual spot-check of INFO-level logs during
      integration test run).
- [ ] ADR-0018 written and committed.

*End of PRD — Slice 1: Statutory Decision Clocks & Coordinator Workflow Coverage*
